message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas – A Quick Overview** | Topic | Key Points | |-------|------------| | **Primary Authority** | Texas Transportation Code (TTC) – the statutory framework governing all road‑use rules in the state. | | **Speed Limits** | • 55 mph on rural interstates, 65 mph on urban interstates, 45 mph on rural highways, 35 mph on urban highways.
• Local municipalities may set lower limits; posted signs are mandatory. | | **Seat‑belt & Child‑seat Requirements** | • All occupants must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child safety seat or booster. | | **Cell‑phone Use** | • Hand‑held phone use while driving is prohibited (except for emergency calls).
• Hands‑free devices are allowed. | | **DUI / Alcohol Limits** | • Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of 0.08% or higher is illegal for drivers over 21.
• Lower limits apply to commercial drivers (0.04%) and drivers under 21 (0.02%). | | **Traffic Signal & Stop‑Sign Rules** | • Red light: stop before the line; proceed only when the signal turns green.
• Yellow light: treat as a stop sign if you cannot safely cross. | | **Right‑of‑Way** | • At uncontrolled intersections, the vehicle on the right has priority unless otherwise indicated.
• Pedestrians have priority at crosswalks. | | **Lane‑Changing & Passing** | • Must signal, check mirrors, and ensure safe gaps.
• Passing on the right is prohibited except in specific circumstances (e.g., passing a stopped vehicle). | | **School‑Zone Speed Limits** | • 25 mph during school hours; 15 mph during special events. | | **Parking Regulations** | • No parking within 20 ft of a fire hydrant, 30 ft of a stop sign, or 15 ft of a crosswalk.
• Parking on sidewalks is prohibited unless marked. | | **Vehicle Equipment** | • Headlights must be on from sunset to sunrise.
• Tires must have adequate tread depth (2 / 32 in. for passenger cars). | | **Penalties & Enforcement** | • Fines, points on driver’s license, possible license suspension, and/or jail time depending on violation severity.
• Texas DPS issues citations; repeat offenders may face harsher penalties. | ### How to Find Specific Statutes 1. **Texas Transportation Code** – Available online at the Texas Legislature’s website. *Example:* Section 545.001 covers speed limits; Section 545.021 covers seat‑belt laws. 2. **Texas Department of Public Safety (DPS)** – Provides fact sheets, driver handbooks, and enforcement guidelines. 3. **Local County Ordinances** – Some counties (e.g., Harris, Dallas) have additional regulations, especially regarding parking and local speed limits. ### Common Violations & Typical Penalties (Illustrative) | Violation | Typical Fine | Points | Possible License Suspension | |-----------|--------------|--------|-----------------------------| | Speeding (up to 10 mph over limit) | $100–$200 | 1–2 | None | | Speeding (over 20 mph over limit) | $200–$400 | 3–4 | 30 days | | DUI (BAC 0.08–0.15) | $500–$1,000 | 4–5 | 90 days | | DUI (BAC >0.15) | $1,000+ | 6–7 | 180 days | | Cell‑phone use while driving | $150–$300 | 1 | None | | Failure to yield to pedestrians | $200–$400 | 2–3 | 30 days | > **Note:** These figures are approximate; actual penalties depend on the county, prior record, and court discretion. ### Resources | Resource | Link | |----------|------| | Texas Legislature – Transportation Code | https://statutes.capitol.texas.gov/ | | Texas DPS – Driver Handbook | https://www.txdps.state.tx.us/ | | Texas DPS – Traffic Law Enforcement | https://www.txdps.state.tx.us/traffic/ | | Texas Courts – Case Law Database | https://www.txcourts.gov/ | --- #### Quick Tips for Safe Driving in Texas - **Always obey posted signs** – they reflect local ordinances that may differ from state law. - **Check your mirrors** before changing lanes or turning. - **Use headlights** from sunset to sunrise, even on clear days. - **Keep a safe following distance** – at least 2 seconds behind the vehicle ahead. - **Avoid distractions** – hands‑free only if you must use a phone. If you need more detailed information on a specific statute or want to see how a particular law is applied in recent cases, let me know!
